overview: CapitaLand Investment Limited (CLI) is a Singapore-headquartered global real estate investment manager, listed in September 2021 after CapitaLand Limited split its development arm (now privately held CapitaLand Development/CapitaLand Group) from its fee-income-generating investment management business. CLI is not a developer or a REIT itself; it earns recurring fees for managing capital on behalf of third parties -- running eight listed REITs/business trusts (including CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust, CapitaLand Ascendas REIT and CapitaLand Ascott Trust), a private funds platform, and The Ascott Limited lodging management business -- while holding balance-sheet stakes (sponsor holdings, co-investments and directly held property) that support that fee franchise. At end-FY2025 CLI reported S$125 billion in funds under management (FUM) across more than 270 cities in 45 countries, with Singapore and China its two core markets (52% of FY2025 revenue).

business_model.summary: CLI runs two linked businesses: a Fee Business (FRB) comprising fund/REIT management, private funds management, lodging management and commercial/asset management, which earns recurring and event-driven fees scaled to FUM; and an Investment Business (REIB) comprising directly held investment properties and strategic/sponsor stakes in the funds and REITs it manages, which provides balance-sheet income, co-investment alignment and a pipeline of assets for capital recycling into its funds. Management's explicit strategy is to shift the earnings mix toward FRB (asset-light, higher-multiple fee income) and shrink REIB's share through continued divestment, particularly in China.

revenue_streams.name: Investment Business (REIB) - property income, portfolio gains, revaluations

business_model.customer_type: Institutional/wholesale capital (pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurers, private wealth) as fund LPs and REIT unitholders; B2B property owners/occupiers for commercial and lodging management services
business_model.geographic_mix: Singapore and China together ~52% of FY2025 revenue and ~67% of total assets; other developed markets (e.g. Japan, Australia, Europe, US) ~34% of revenue; other emerging markets (e.g. India, Southeast Asia) ~14% of revenue

main_competitors: Blackstone/Brookfield (global alternative asset managers in APAC real estate)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest real estate investment manager in Asia Pacific by AUM -- the 2026 ANREV/INREV/NCREIF Fund Manager Survey ranked CLI first in APAC real estate AUM, overtaking ESR Group, which had led in 2024. CLI is also the largest REIT sponsor/manager in Asia by market capitalisation, with 8 listed REITs/business trusts across Singapore, Malaysia, China and Japan.

moat_factors.factor: Scale of FUM and sponsor pipeline
moat_factors.description: S$125B FUM (targeting S$200B by 2028) with a captive acquisition pipeline from the former parent CapitaLand Development (private) and third-party mandates, giving CLI first-look access to assets its funds can acquire

Eight listed REITs/trusts across four exchanges provide permanent capital vehicles, recurring management fees independent of fundraising cycles, and a route for asset recycling (selling balance-sheet or private-fund assets into the REITs)

Three-decades-plus operating history, CapitaLand brand recognition in Asia, and REIT management performance (FY2025 Singapore-listed funds delivered 15.6-29.9% total unitholder returns, outperforming the FTSE ST REIT Index's 16.9%)

CLI targets 15-20% sponsor stakes in its directly-managed listed funds, aligning incentives with unitholders and supporting capital efficiency, but this also ties balance-sheet capital and earnings to REIT unit price and NAV movements

CLI listed China's first international-sponsored retail C-REIT (CapitaLand Commercial C-REIT) in September 2025 and a second C-REIT in 2H2026, plus an onshore RMB Master Fund, giving early access to China's nascent onshore REIT market as a capital-recycling channel

weaknesses: Still carries meaningful legacy balance-sheet real estate (REIB), which is capital-intensive, cyclical and subject to revaluation swings -- unlike pure asset-light managers

China concentration: a large share of remaining REIB assets are in China, where revaluation losses and discounted divestments (circa 13-20% below book in recent sales) have repeatedly dragged down total PATMI
Private funds management and lodging management are still sub-scale relative to listed funds and are loss-making/low-margin while being built out, requiring continued growth investment

Earnings volatility: total PATMI fell 70% YoY in FY2025 (S$479M to S$145M) due to portfolio gains/revaluation swings, illustrating that reported profit is far less stable than the underlying fee business

growth_drivers: FUM growth target of S$200 billion by 2028 (from S$125B at FY2025, S$128B at H1 2026), driven by new fund launches, follow-on fundraising in existing listed/private funds, and new REIT listings
Operating earnings target of over S$1 billion by 2028-2030 (from S$539M operating PATMI in FY2025), underpinned by the fee-income mix shift

Private funds management scaling across lodging and living, logistics and self-storage, real estate credit and data centres -- fundraising nearly doubled to S$4.9B in FY2025, aided by the 40% stake in SC Capital Partners (SCCP) and in Wingate Group

Lodging management (The Ascott Limited) targeting S$500 million fee revenue (from S$350M in FY2025, a six-year ~15% CAGR), with record signings (~19,000 units in FY2025) and expansion into resorts, branded residences and franchise/conversion models

China onshore REIT market entry (CapitaLand Commercial C-REIT listed September 2025; second C-REIT targeted 2H2026) and an RMB Master Fund, providing a structural outlet to recycle China balance-sheet assets into permanent capital vehicles

Accelerating capital recycling: management has identified S$7-9 billion of embedded value in non-core legacy funds/balance-sheet assets (about two-thirds in China) for divestment, reinvestment, debt reduction or shareholder returns
Potential new REIT listings in strategic markets to deepen the permanent-capital platform and improve earnings resilience
AI/digital initiatives generating measurable fee and cost efficiencies (>S$12M revenue uplift in FY2025) across the CapitaLand Group

business.risk: Competition from established real asset managers
business.description: Peers such as ESR, Mapletree, Keppel, GLP and global alternative managers compete for the same institutional capital and acquisition opportunities; CLI must keep attracting capital and sourcing deals to sustain FUM growth

Singapore and China are CLI's two core markets (52% of FY2025 revenue, ~67% of total assets); continued softness in Chinese commercial property has driven large unrealised revaluation losses (-S$439M in FY2025) and divestments at discounts to book value
Ascott's RevPAU and occupancy are sensitive to global travel demand, geopolitical disruption and macro conditions; China lodging RevPAU fell 3% YoY in FY2025 even as other regions grew

business.risk: Execution risk on private funds and lodging scale-up
business.description: Growth investment in private funds and lodging management platforms is currently diluting near-term fee-business margins (private funds EBITDA margin 34% vs listed funds 47%; lodging margin compressed to 36% from 37%)

financial.risk: Interest rate and funding cost sensitivity
financial.description: 28% of CLI's debt is floating rate; implied interest cost improved to 3.9% in FY2025 from 4.4%, but higher-for-longer rates would raise finance costs and could pressure REIT valuations in which CLI holds sponsor stakes

Net debt-to-equity rose from 0.35x (FY2024) to 0.43x (FY2025) and further to 0.45x at H1 2026, driven by net loan drawdowns and sustainability-linked bond issuance; debt headroom of ~S$6.4B to a 0.9x covenant ceiling provides buffer but reduces flexibility if asset values keep falling

Revenue and asset values span SGD, RMB, JPY, MYR, AUD, EUR, USD, GBP and others; currency translation swings materially affected FY2025 comprehensive income (e.g. -S$158M translation loss and -S$57M cash flow hedge movement in H1 2025 alone, reversing in H1 2026)

Reported PATMI is heavily influenced by non-cash revaluation gains/losses on investment properties and portfolio gains on divestments, both of which swung sharply between FY2024 and FY2025 (total PATMI -70% YoY) and obscure the underlying fee-business trend

regulatory.risk: Fund management and REIT manager regulation
regulatory.description: CLI's fund management and REIT management subsidiaries are regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore and equivalent regulators in China, Malaysia and Japan; regulatory changes to REIT leverage limits, fee structures or fund manager licensing could affect economics

regulatory.risk: China capital controls and onshore REIT regulation
regulatory.description: CLI's growing onshore China REIT/fund strategy (C-REIT listings, RMB Master Fund) depends on evolving, still-nascent Chinese REIT regulation and capital account rules that could change the pace or terms of future listings and repatriation
Operating across 45 countries exposes CLI to evolving tax, anti-money-laundering, sanctions and data protection regimes, requiring ongoing compliance investment

macro.description: Private real estate fundraising only returned to growth in 2025 (first annual increase since 2021, per PERE) after a prolonged downturn; a renewed slowdown in institutional allocations to real estate would directly reduce CLI's fee-related revenue growth
Management flags heightened geopolitical tensions and trade policy volatility across APAC as a headwind to investor sentiment, capital flows and asset values in FY2026
Macro slowdowns or shocks (e.g. pandemics, regional conflict) directly affect Ascott's lodging RevPAU and signing/opening pace

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global private real estate fundraising rebounded 29% YoY to US$222.2 billion in 2025 (first annual increase since 2021, per PERE), with capital continuing to favour scaled managers with established track records. The 2026 ANREV/INREV/NCREIF survey put global real estate AUM at US$4.5 trillion (+19% YoY) and ranked CLI first in APAC real estate AUM. Singapore REITs benefited from an easing domestic interest rate environment in 2025, while global-focused REITs managed higher or stable borrowing costs in other markets.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high for the REIB/balance-sheet portion (property valuations and portfolio gains move with real estate cycles and interest rates); lower and more resilient for the fee business, which scales with FUM and is less sensitive to short-term valuation swings, though event-driven fees depend on transaction/fundraising activity
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate direct exposure via ~28% floating-rate debt and finance costs; higher indirect exposure via REIT unit prices/valuations (in which CLI holds sponsor stakes), capitalisation rates used in property revaluations, and investor appetite for real estate fundraising
key_input_costs: Property operating and maintenance costs (lodging, retail, office)
Staff costs and talent retention in competitive fund management labour market

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 revenue of S$1,018M (-2% YoY) but PATMI up 14% YoY to S$327M; fee revenue rose roughly 20%; FUM grew to S$128B (+2% from FY2025's S$125B); gross divestments of ~S$5.0B year-to-date across Singapore, India and China, including gains from CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust and CapitaLand India Growth Fund II

CLI listed a second China onshore retail REIT (CNY3.15 billion China Commercial Private REIT) on 11 August 2026, with a further C-REIT listing targeted for 2H2026, extending CLI's onshore RMB fundraising and capital-recycling channel in China

Management has identified S$7-9 billion of embedded value in non-core legacy funds and balance-sheet assets for recycling, roughly two-thirds in China and 30-40% in private funds, with proceeds earmarked for reinvestment, debt reduction and potential shareholder returns

FY2025 operating PATMI rose 6% YoY to S$539M, but total PATMI fell 70% YoY to S$145M on higher China revaluation losses (-S$439M) and lower portfolio gains; FUM reached S$125B; FRR grew 6% to S$1.23B; ordinary dividend held flat at 12.0 Singapore cents (no repeat of FY2024's 6.5-cent special dividend from the CICT unit distribution)

CLI listed CapitaLand Commercial C-REIT (CLCR) on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, China's first international-sponsored retail C-REIT, achieving 254.5x institutional and 535.2x retail subscription coverage

Completed acquisition of a 40% stake in SC Capital Partners Group (SCCP), gaining a foothold in Japan's J-REIT market via Japan Hotel REIT and expanding private funds deal origination and institutional investor access; also advanced the Wingate Group strategic investment

Sold a 4.88% stake in CapitaLand Ascott Trust (CLAS), triggering deconsolidation of CLAS from subsidiary to associate -- a structural change that reduces reported revenue/EBITDA on a consolidated basis going forward and was a major driver of FY2025's YoY comparisons

Brokers were split post-FY2025 results: Citi (Buy, S$3.40 target) and OCBC flagged the results as a miss on China revaluation losses and softer divestment pace, while still seeing a credible path to S$150-160B FUM; CGS International, Maybank, DBS, UOB Kay Hian and Phillip Securities maintained Buy/Add ratings with targets clustered S$3.40-4.30

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (13 March 2026) and H1 2026 results (reported ~August/September 2026)

items.notes: Long-standing target first announced February 2024 (double FUM within five years from ~S$91-99B base); FUM was S$125B at FY2025 and S$128B at H1 2026, roughly 64% of the way to target
Set out at the November 2024 Investor Day; FY2025 operating PATMI was S$539 million, requiring continued double-digit-equivalent compounding to reach target
FY2025 lodging fee revenue was S$350 million (six-year CAGR ~15%); management expects the sizeable signed pipeline to convert to fee revenue as properties open
FY2025 ordinary dividend held flat at 12.0 Singapore cents per share (total 12.0 cents vs 18.5 cents in FY2024, which included a one-off 6.5-cent special distribution in specie of CICT units)

items.target: acceleration in FY2026 from FY2025's S$3.1 billion
items.notes: Management explicitly guided to faster divestment pace in FY2026, including evaluating portfolio/structural solutions for China assets; H1 2026 already showed ~S$5.0B of gross divestments year-to-date, and management has flagged a S$7-9B pool of non-core legacy assets (about two-thirds China) for recycling

items.period: FY2025 actual, used as a run-rate reference
items.notes: Fund management FRR-to-FUM ratio improved to 52 bps (from 48 bps) reflecting the growing contribution of private funds and SCCP

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Miguel Ko and Group CEO Lee Chee Koon describe CLI's ambition as becoming 'a scaled, asset-light, global investment manager anchored by resilient, recurring fee income.' They characterise the FY2026 operating environment as 'generally supportive, though global uncertainties warrant continued vigilance,' citing APAC geopolitical uncertainty and trade policy volatility. Management is explicit that it will 'accelerate divestments' -- especially in China -- 'while maintaining disciplined and value-accretive deployment,' and points to the CapitaLand Commercial C-REIT listing and the onshore RMB Master Fund as structural pathways supporting a 'domestic-for-domestic' China capital-recycling strategy. On lodging, management expects Ascott to keep scaling as 'a core asset-light growth engine' supported by a large pipeline of signed-but-not-yet-open units.

bull_case: Clear, quantified strategic targets (S$200B FUM by 2028, >S$1B operating earnings by 2028-2030) with FUM already up from S$91B at listing to S$128B at H1 2026, demonstrating consistent execution

Asset-light fee business is structurally resilient and growing (FRR +6% YoY in FY2025, fee revenue +~20% YoY in H1 2026) even as the volatile legacy balance-sheet business shrinks, improving the quality and multiple of earnings over time

Ranked #1 real estate AUM manager in Asia Pacific (2026 survey), with a diversified eight-REIT listed platform, a scaling private funds business (SCCP, Wingate) and an asset-light lodging platform (Ascott) targeting S$500M in fee revenue

Large, identified pool of capital-recycling opportunities (S$7-9B of non-core/legacy assets) gives multiple levers for value realisation, debt reduction or capital returns independent of broader market conditions

First-mover position in China's nascent onshore REIT market (two C-REIT listings, RMB Master Fund) offers a structural, domestic-currency exit route for China assets that pure foreign-currency divestment cannot match
bear_case: China exposure remains large and the divestment path has required discounts of 13-20% to book value, with further revaluation losses likely while the Chinese commercial property market stays soft

Reported PATMI is highly volatile and sentiment-driving (down 70% YoY in FY2025) due to non-cash revaluation swings and lumpy portfolio gains, making the stock's headline earnings a poor read of the underlying fee business and a recurring source of negative headlines/analyst downgrades
Net debt-to-equity has risen for two consecutive periods (0.35x to 0.43x to 0.45x) as divestment proceeds have been slower than planned, reducing the pace of deleveraging management had signalled

Private funds management and lodging management are still sub-scale and margin-dilutive while being built out, so near-term fee-business EBITDA margin has compressed (FRB margin fell from ~50% toward the high-30s/40s as private funds/lodging mix grows)

Execution risk on the S$200B FUM / S$1B operating earnings targets: achieving them requires sustained fundraising in an uneven global capital-raising environment, successful integration of SCCP/Wingate, and successful conversion of Ascott's signed pipeline into opened, fee-generating units
